premise.claim: On the base branch, app pods of FUSE-less cache runtimes have no way to receive the runtime config that stage 1 (#6191) writes into the runtime ConfigMap, and the webhook lacks RBAC to read cacheruntimes at all.

findings.claim: On helm upgrade over an existing installation (forceReplacePluginsProfile defaults to false), plugins-profile.yaml's lookup keeps the old webhook-plugins ConfigMap without the clientless group, while webhookconfiguration.yaml unconditionally adds the clientless.fluid.io rule; pods labeled fluid.io/inject=true are then intercepted but admitted with zero injection, silently.
tests: pkg/webhook/handler/mutating/clientless_harness_test.go#F1-canary (Go consequence: empty clientless handler list -> no-op)
scripts/chart_lookup_branch_sim.go (chart half: real template + real values.yaml, stubbed lookup)

findings.claim: When the runtime config ConfigMap is missing (not-yet-created or informer lag on the plugin's cached client), the plugin returns a plain non-retryable error; Handle() logs it and admits the pod without any injection - failurePolicy: Fail gives no protection because the webhook itself answers Allowed.
tests: pkg/webhook/handler/mutating/clientless_harness_test.go#F2-canary (MutatePod error is NOT NeedRetryWithApiReaderError, pod left untouched)

findings.claim: Happy path: MutatePod routes a fluid.io/inject=true + fluid.io/datasets pod to the clientless plugin and injects volume + readOnly mount + FLUID_RUNTIME_CONFIG_PATH_<DS> + done label.
A dataset named in the annotation that does not exist fails collection with a retryable error, which after the direct-reader retry rejects pod creation (matches the documented behavior).

harnessBites.F2: temporarily wrapped the plugin's not-found error in NewNeedRetryWithApiReaderError; the F2 canary flipped to FAILED as expected; production code reverted (diff clean)
harnessBites.F1: the CONTROL spec in the same run registers the with-clientless profile and observes injection - the canary and control differ only in the profile, proving the test detects the upgrade-state difference

live.reason: Skipped per this review round's configuration (unit + integration only). A live cluster WAS reachable from the review host (2 nodes, v1.36.2-aliyun) but it is a shared cluster, not a dedicated test environment.
live.liveNote: On a dedicated cluster, the L3 check for F1 would be: helm upgrade an existing fluid install with this chart, create a pod with labels fluid.io/inject=true + annotation fluid.io/datasets, and observe no FLUID_RUNTIME_CONFIG_PATH_* env and no webhook log line about RuntimeConfigInjector.
